name: found_ai_ay
intended: You found a new sound! Look, here is its petal, shining through the mist. This is a spelling of the sound... /ae/ It's two letters, but it's one sound. ...like in rain, tail and nail. You found a new gem! It's a spelling of the sound... /ae/ This is another way to spell the sound... /ae/ It's two letters, but it's one sound. ...like in tray, day and say. Now you know two ways to spell... /ae/
joins: Smooth transitions with well-paced natural pauses around the sound presentations and examples.
sounds: The /ae/ vowel sound is articulated clearly and cleanly each time.
fix: None needed; the pacing, audio joins, and phonetic accuracy are excellent.

name: victory_ai
intended: You won the gem! It's going into its petal! Look! Your new gem goes here, in its petal. This is another way to spell the sound... /ae/ It's two letters, but it's one sound. ...like in rain, tail and nail. Now you know two ways to spell... /ae/
joins: The flow is generally smooth, though the transition right after the first /ae/ sound into 'It's two letters' comes in slightly abruptly.
sounds: The phoneme /ae/ (/eɪ/) is clean, accurate, and pronounced clearly without any extraneous vowel or 'uh'.
wrong_words: None; matches the intended script exactly.
fix: Add a slight pause (around 200–300 ms) after the first /ae/ sound before 'It's two letters' to let the phoneme breathe.

name: victory_m_home
intended: You won the gem! It's going into its petal! Look! Your new gem goes here, in its petal. This is the way we spell... /m/ ...in mat. We see this spelling in man and map. All the gems are in! The petal flies back onto the World Flower!
joins: The joins are well-paced, though there is a minor tone/energy shift between the explanatory phonics section and the enthusiastic narrative lines.
sounds: The /m/ phoneme is clean and pronounced correctly without an added schwa.
fix: Slightly smooth the acoustic transition around 0:10-0:14 where the instructional tone drops in energy compared to the surrounding celebratory lines.

name: found_igh
intended: You found a new gem! It's a spelling of the sound... /ie/ This is another way to spell the sound... /ie/ It's three letters, but it's just one sound. Say that sound with me! /ie/ ...like in light, night and high. Now you know two ways to spell... /ie/
joins: Smooth transitions with well-timed, natural pedagogical pauses before each target sound.
sounds: The /ie/ sound is cleanly articulated as a pure vowel sound throughout.
fix: None needed; the delivery is engaging, warm, and well-paced for early phonics instruction.

name: practised_ready
intended: Look! Your gem filled up with ninja power. A gem is glowing! It's ready for a gem battle.
joins: Natural pacing and smooth pitch continuity; the pause between 'ninja power' and 'A gem is glowing!' is slightly long but acceptable.
sounds: Clean and clear pronunciations throughout with no audio artifacts.
fix: Slightly reduce the pause between 'ninja power' and 'A gem is glowing' by about 0.2 to 0.3 seconds for a snappier flow.

name: world_same_s
intended: Let's visit the World Flower! Every shining petal is a sound that you know! Different spellings of... /s/ ...but it's the same sound! "sit" ...and... "dress" New sounds are hiding in this land. Let's go and find them!
joins: Smooth transitions with natural pauses and consistent warmth and acoustic tone throughout.
sounds: The /s/ is cleanly produced as a pure hiss with no schwa.
fix: None needed; the pacing, tone, and pronunciation are well suited for a young learner.

name: found_th_dh
intended: You found a new sound! Look, here is its petal, shining through the mist. This is the way we spell... /dh/ ...in this. It's two letters, but it's one sound. We see this spelling in that and them. The same spelling can sometimes be... /th/ ...in... "moth" ...and sometimes... /dh/ ...in... "this"
joins: The unvoiced /th/ at 00:20 cuts in abruptly, followed by an awkward drop in pitch and energy on 'in moth'. The /dh/ sound at 00:08 also feels slightly clipped before 'in this'.
sounds: The phonemes /dh/ and /th/ are accurate and pure with no trailing 'uh', though /th/ at 00:20 is slightly loud and breathy.
fix: Smooth the transition and match the pitch/intonation between 'be...', /th/, and 'in moth' so it sounds like one continuous sentence.
